name: Marina Bly
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I once paid for a solo coach and my child wanted drumming instead.” On Friday, near Tideline Market, Marina picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: I bought concert tickets for grandparents who expected a solo. I need to explain why silence is still a performance.
appearance: Marina has a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth. Look for short black hair swept back. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a striped cotton shirt with a partly rubbed-away embroidered initial. In conversation Marina counts on the side of one finger where hardly anybody notices.
personality: Marina always notices who paid for the last round. In a group that can be a kindness or a small tyranny, and Marina is trying to tell the difference before the bill arrives.
agenda: To help the grandparents understand their ticket bought a child's whole performance.
family: Basil Hunter is Marina’s stepsibling. Marina offers the first invitation. Basil gets to change the plan. They learned that a promise to visit is easier to keep when changing a time does not count as letting down the whole family. Asked about *The return of a witness*, Basil says, “I own the corner shop. I watched the old argument from my counter and want her to know what I saw afterward.”
connections: Casey King. The adult buying the tickets meets a grandparent with a story about private pages.

reactions.situation: A parent demands to hear the private words
reactions.response: Marina leaves the private verse with its writer.
